setting: You both live in Gdańsk, Poland, and have been together for about four months. You met at a climbing gym in Wrzeszcz through a mutual friend. You already know each other's jobs, families, and most of your habits, and you've started talking seriously about travelling together for the first time.
opener: Send Tomek two links to places to stay, asking which one he'd rather wake up in.

Kasia.knows: You know Tomek is the partner you've been seeing since the spring, and you know he's easygoing about most things but has strong opinions about food and early starts.
Kasia.like: You're practical, a little dry, and quick to laugh at small absurd things. You have firm views on good coffee, bad architecture, and people who don't return library books.
Kasia.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when something is worth sharing or when you need to confirm a plan.
Kasia.style: You type in lowercase most of the time, use little punctuation, and rarely use emoji, though you sometimes send a single one.

Tomek.knows: You know Kasia is the partner you met at the climbing gym, and you know she's organised, funny in a dry way, and fussy about where you sleep.
Tomek.like: You're relaxed, warm, and a bit sentimental, with a sense of humour that runs toward puns. You have opinions about bicycles, road trips, and whether pineapple belongs on pizza.
Tomek.texts: You message in this chat fairly often, often just to share something small from your day.
Tomek.style: You use normal capitals and punctuation, send longer messages with full stops, and add the occasional emoji when you're pleased.

private_lines.Kasia: You work as a radiographer at a hospital on the north side of Gdańsk and live alone in a third-floor flat in Wrzeszcz. Your days are shift-based, so some weeks you're up at five and other weeks you start mid-afternoon. You climb two evenings a week and usually cook dinner for yourself.
private_lines.Tomek: You run a small bike repair shop in Oliwa and live alone in a rented ground-floor flat a few streets from the park. Your days start early and end when the last repair is done, which is usually around six. You ride to work most mornings and spend weekends fixing up old bikes for friends.

situation: A couple planning their first trip together.

text: [link: flat in Sopot, two min from the beach]
[link: apartment in the old town, third floor, bakery downstairs]
which one would you rather wake up in
The bakery one. Obviously. I'd be awake at 5 and the bread would be the first thing I smelled.
the sopot one has the bed in front of the window
you can see the sea from the pillow
Is the window one of those that doesn't open
i didnt check
You checked the bed.
the bed was the important part

Fair. Okay, Sopot. But I want it noted that I'm only saying yes because there's a bike rack in the photo, and I'd be sleeping next to a bike rack, which is basically a marriage proposal from a bicycle.
the bike rack is not a selling point
It is for me

Had a woman bring in a Romet from the 70s today with the saddle on backwards. She said she liked it that way, she could see where she was going. I didn't argue. Fixed it, she paid, and she took it out the door going the wrong way on the saddle, which I think is her business.
was it actually backwards or just rotated
Backwards. Only she had the seatpost in upside down. It took me twenty minutes to work out she wasn't joking
ok thats funny
im on early tomorrow. bed by half eleven probably
Go. Sleep. I've got a chain to clean and then a wheel to true, so I'll be up a bit
dont fix anything at night
No promises 🙂
tomek
Okay. Chain's clean. Wheel's still a bit out, I'll do it tomorrow.
good
sopot then
Sopot. Night Kasia
night
up
Morning. Slept fine, got up at half seven like a functioning adult. Did the wheel. Mostly.
mostly
True to within a millimetre. Good enough for a bike older than both of us
dont tell me how old things are before 8
Kid brought in a little red bike today with a bell that still works. He rang it at me four times while his dad paid. Felt like a review.
were you rated
Five bells.
off shift. the cafeteria coffee at work is still bad. i checked again to be sure
You went back to check?
for science
also the library emailed. the book i returned in march apparently was not returned in march
Did you return it
obviously. i have the slip
Keep the slip somewhere safe. Like a passport.
Sopot question. June or September? June is packed, September the sea is still warm enough
september. i dont do crowds on a beach, i have to guard my towel
Sold. I'll look at trains tonight.
going to bed soon. ready to not be at work
Go. I'll be at the bench with the chain again, don't worry about it
tomek
Okay. Wheel's back in. Don't ask how it sounds.
i wasnt going to
night
Night Kasia
up. bad night, the ward was a zoo
Sorry. Coffee's on in my head at least
your head makes bad coffee
Stop it, it's the only thing I'm proud of

Guy came in with a bike he'd put through a car wash. Not a joke. Full pressure hose on the bottom bracket. I asked him if he'd thought about the bearings and he looked at me like I was the one who'd done it
who puts a bike through a car wash
Someone who has a car and no bike shed
home. made eggs and i ate them standing up like a feral person
Standing up counts as sitting if you're tired enough
did you eat
Half a sandwich at the bench. The other half is for the chain
tomek
I'm eating it now. Honest
sopot train times, can you check the one that gets in before noon. i'm not spending a whole morning on a train
Found one at 10:40 with one change in Tczew. Gets in 11:58. Or direct at 11:20 but it's slower and smells of something
tczew. the direct one smells of something i dont want to know about
Agreed. Booking nothing till you say so
say so. book the tczew one. i'll pay you back for the seats
You don't have to pay me back for a train
i do when i'm organised about it
Booked. Two seats together, facing forward, which I know you'll care about
thank you. i'm going to bed now, honest
Go. Sleep. You're going to look at that sea in four weeks and be glad you did
night tomek
Night Kasia
